title: Jabra’s Latest Hearing Aids Are Outstanding but Incremental
gist: Wired rates Jabra's new Enhance Select M3 over-the-counter hearing aid 8/10: outstanding quality but an incremental update at an unchanged $1,995 launch price, with a bulky case and weak streaming.

insights.claim: Jabra replaced its entire hearing-aid lineup (Enhance Select 700, 500, 300, 50R) with the M3, M2 and M1, only a year or two after the old models; the changes are mostly under the hood and hardly extreme.
insights.speaker: Christopher Null
insights.so_what: Rapid product refresh cycles in the OTC hearing-aid category compress resale and early-adopter value.

insights.claim: The M3 starts at $1,995, the same launch price as the Jabra 700, with the M2 at $1,695 and M1 at $1,195; the reviewer expects a roughly $200 cut within months, and says a prescription aid of this quality would likely cost twice as much.
insights.speaker: Christopher Null
insights.so_what: Pricing is flat generation to generation; wait for discounts or buy the cheaper tiers.

insights.claim: The reviewer concludes the M3 is the most advanced over-the-counter hearing aid available, but buyers on modest budgets will do nearly as well with the M2 or M1.
insights.speaker: Christopher Null
insights.so_what: Marginal value of the top tier is low relative to its price premium.

insights.claim: The M3 adds two exclusive SoundScape features, a revamped autofocus that 'locks onto' speech in noisy settings (moderately effective) and an adaptive listening mode, but environmental modes were not very useful and manual tuning worked best.
insights.speaker: Christopher Null
insights.so_what: Incremental software gains rather than a hardware leap.
insights.locator: Jabra calls its audio enhancement system SoundScape

insights.claim: Bluetooth streaming remains Jabra's weak spot despite Auracast support: music and movie audio are washed out below top volume and ambient noise ruins the experience.
insights.speaker: Christopher Null
insights.so_what: Streaming quality is an unresolved competitive gap for the category.
insights.locator: Bluetooth streaming quality has never been Jabra’s strong suit

insights.claim: Jabra's service remains a differentiator: three years of audiologist access by video chat and a built-in audiogram self-test, while the large case, three recharges, is unchanged and a full charge lasts 24 hours.
insights.speaker: Christopher Null
insights.so_what: Service bundling supports the direct-to-consumer model versus clinic-based prescription aids.
